name: Heaphy Track
why: From the Aorere valley over the open tussock of Gouland Downs and down the Heaphy River to nīkau palms and the West Coast surf.
book: Huts and campsites must be booked all year round. Brown Hut is at the road end up the Aorere valley from Collingwood; Kohaihai is 15 km north of Karamea. The ends are far apart by road: book a shuttle or flight back. Mountain bikes 1 May-30 Nov.
water: Tap water at huts and campsites, untreated: boil it.
dangers: Gouland Downs is featureless in mist: stay on the track.
Floods near Saxon Hut, along the Heaphy River and at Cave Stream after heavy rain: wait in a hut.
Do not swim at the Heaphy or Kohaihai river mouths: strong currents and rips.
Large waves can close the coastal section at high tide in rough seas.
turnaround: If the Heaphy River is flooded, stay at James Mackay or Heaphy Hut until it drops.

points.name: Brown Hut
points.note: Road end in the Aorere valley. The track climbs gradually on an old road survey line.

points.name: Perry Saddle Hut
points.note: First night at 880 m, 17.5 km in; Flanagans Corner (915 m), the highest point, is 30 min before.

points.name: Gouland Downs
points.note: Open tussock downs and the small Gouland Downs Hut. Great spotted kiwi live here.

points.name: James Mackay Hut
points.note: Second night, on a terrace with the Tasman Sea 15 km west and 750 m below.

points.name: Heaphy Hut, river mouth
points.note: Third night by the Heaphy River mouth, among nīkau palms. No swimming.

points.name: Kohaihai
points.note: After 16.2 km of coastal forest and Scotts Beach: shelter and car park, 15 km from Karamea.
